No CITATION.cff, CodeMeta, or package structure is evidenced. nimbleCarbon is a third-party dependency and is not counted as a substitute.

barriers: The deposit contents (file list, formats, README) cannot be checked from admissible evidence. Supplementary files were deliberately withheld, and the evidence pack has no file manifest, so completeness rests on the paper's statement that 'All data and R scripts' are deposited on Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.10782942.

Inventory (16 datasets). Principal datasets, all Tier 0 in the open Zenodo deposit: simulated datasets 1a, 1b, and 2; the Japan 14C compilation (n = 551, 215 sites); the Britain wheat/barley/hazelnut 14C compilation (n = 928, 314 sites); and the British burial 14C compilation (cremation n = 1417, inhumation n = 1119). Upstream sources: Kudo et al. 2023; the Crema et al. 2022 rice database; Bevan et al. 2017; Bloxam 2020; Bloxam and Parker Pearson 2022; Healy 2012; Mallick and Reich 2023 (AADR); Olalde et al. 2018; Wilkin 2013; and Willis et al. 2016. The paper states that the records used from each upstream source are in the open deposit, so each is classed as accessible (Tier 0) through the deposit.

Some upstream sources are hard to reach in their original form. Healy 2012 is a chapter in an Oxbow edited volume (Prehistoric Society Research Paper 4), a paywalled monograph. Bloxam 2020 (UCL) and Wilkin 2013 (University of Birmingham) are theses, and the paper does not say whether they are openly accessible. This limits checking the compilation against its originals but does not block reproduction, because the records used are stated to be in the deposit. It is not counted against coverage.
The GitHub mirror records no licence and has no persistence entitlement (evidence pack). The persistent copy is the Zenodo archive.

A1.evidence: The DOI resolves over HTTPS (pack http_status 200; Zenodo access_right 'open'). Data completeness is 'complete' (16/16 accessible) on the paper's statement that 'All data and R scripts' are archived at the DOI, so the A1 completeness override does not apply.

A1_1.evidence: Retrieval uses HTTPS and DOI resolution (https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.10782942; pack request URLs over HTTPS), which are open, free, and universally implementable.

A1_2.evidence: The Zenodo record has access_right 'open' (pack). This is a fully open resource needing no authentication, which satisfies A1.2 under v2.1. No access control is warranted (published radiocarbon dates, no human-subject or CARE-sensitive data).

A2.evidence: The paper and pack are silent on what happens after withdrawal, so this rests on rung (ii). Row 2 (Zenodo): 'tombstone page on withdrawal with DOI and URL retained ... metadata always publicly accessible'. Row 1 (DataCite): the DOI string is undeletable and Handle-resolvable. The DataCite record is confirmed in the pack.

F1.evidence: The deposit has its own persistent identifier (PID). p. 7: 'All data and R scripts are available on https://github.com/ercrema/diffusionCurve and permanently archived on https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.10782942.' In the evidence pack, DataCite resolves DOI 10.5281/zenodo.10782942 (state 'findable'), and Zenodo shows concept DOI 10.5281/zenodo.10782942 with version DOI 10.5281/zenodo.10816946. Per the paper, all principal datasets are in this one deposit.

F2.evidence: In the pack, the DataCite record has metadata_record: true (publisher Zenodo, publication_year 2024, resource_type Software), and the Zenodo record also has metadata_record: true. Platform table Row 2 (Zenodo) guarantees a DataCite metadata record, which has structured creators and title. Under the instrument, a deposit with its own PID carries the F subtotal of 4/4. A description is not guaranteed by Row 2 and is not visible in the pack fields.

F3.evidence: Both the DataCite and Zenodo pack records have identifier_in_metadata: true. Row 1 guarantees a DataCite record carrying the DOI.

F4.evidence: The DataCite record state is 'findable' (indexed in the DataCite registry), with publisher Zenodo (pack). Zenodo and DataCite are both listed as searchable registries under F4.

I1.evidence: The data formats are never stated: the paper says only 'All data and R scripts are available...' (p. 7). The pack records have no file or format fields, and no platform-table entitlement covers data format. With the ladder exhausted, data I1 is unscoreable and scores 0. The code language (R) is evidenced, but that does not establish the data representation.

I2.evidence: No controlled vocabulary or ontology (e.g. PeriodO, Getty AAT) is named for coding periods, sites, plant taxa, or burial rite. Periods (Jomon, Yayoi, Beaker, Late Neolithic) and materials are free-text in the paper. The pack and platform table say nothing on this.

I3.evidence: The upstream data sources are cited with typed relations ('collated from the radiocarbon database of Japan (Kudo et al., 2023) and the rice radiocarbon database used in (Crema et al., 2022)'; 'obtained from Bevan et al. (2017)'), but the reference list gives no PIDs for them. The only data source with a DOI is AADR (https://doi.org/10.7910/DVN/FFIDCW). Data are scored conjunctively, so I3 fails for the Japan and Britain-agriculture datasets. The pack records have no related-identifier fields.

R1.evidence: Section 4.1 describes each principal dataset in detail. Quotes: '1479 14C dates on seed remains from Japan (n = 551, from 215 sites...) and Britain (n = 928, from 314 sites)'; 'cumulative calibrated probability mass equal to or larger than 0.5 for the interval 4000-1700 cal BP'; 'rice (n = 203) ... nuts (n = 348)'; 'wheat (n = 261) and barley (n = 130) ... hazelnut (n = 537)'; 'cremation (n = 1417) and inhumation (n = 1119)'. The simulation settings are also given (r, m, mu, phi values; 20-year error).

R1_1.evidence: The paper does not state a data licence. Its CC BY statement covers the article and the Author Accepted Manuscript. The paper is silent, so the licence recorded at the service applies: the Zenodo and DataCite records both list licences ['cc-by-4.0'], with licence_conflicts []. The GitHub mirror records no licence (licences []); that is an absence, not a conflicting assertion, and the persistent deposit is Zenodo. The Row 2 default-licence footnote applies: a default value is still operative.

R1_2.evidence: Provenance is documented. Sources: Kudo et al. 2023, Crema et al. 2022, Bevan et al. 2017, and the burial sources 'collated from different published sources and databases (Bevan et al., 2017; Bloxam, 2020; ... Willis et al., 2016)'. Filtering rules are given, e.g. 'We used a higher probability threshold (0.99 instead of 0.5) to avoid any edge effects'. Simulation generation is described: 'Calendar dates were uniformly generated ... back-calibrated in 14C age, and associated with an arbitrary error of 20 years'. Calibration is stated: 'We used the IntCal20 curve for all models'. Creators are identified through CRediT 'Data curation' for all four authors.

R1_3.evidence: This scores via route (a), a generic metadata schema. The pack confirms the deposit has a DataCite metadata record (metadata_record: true, identifier_in_metadata: true), and Row 2 guarantees DataCite metadata. No domain schema or accredited domain repository is used. IntCal20 is a methodological standard and does not qualify.
